author: Kenley Hargett
title: Franklin Board of Mayor and Aldermen passes Harlin development amid resident concerns - NewsBreak
text:
By Kenley Hargett ,
5 hours ago
FRANKLIN, Tenn. (WKRN) — Passionate pleas from Franklin community members were heard at Tuesday night’s Board of Mayor and Aldermen meeting.
Those pleas were regarding the Harlin development , a proposed residential project that is set to bring more than 100 homes near Highway 31 and Hillview Lane, a hotel and commercial space.
⏩ Read today’s top stories on wkrn.com
One of the biggest issues community members are voicing is more traffic on an already busy road.
“We understand that we can’t limit growth for Franklin; in fact, we embrace that,” a Franklin resident said during the meeting’s public comment period. “But what we also want to do is promote responsible growth that doesn’t degrade our quality of life, especially where we live, our safety, our traffic.”
Memphis and Nashville-based development company Boyle Investment Company is planning to build the Harlin development on the property. The company’s website includes a section that addresses community concerns.
Some improvements they mention include major intersections with an investment of three to four times what is required by the city’s road impact fee calculations. Two other improvements are preserving a tree tunnel and a strong focus on preservation.
📧 Have breaking news come to you: Subscribe to News 2 email alerts →
“That’s why tonight we are asking for your final approval on a project that puts infrastructure first,” Boyle Investment Company’s Adam Ballash said. “This project develops only .67 units an acre, with a mixture of housing.”
Leaders voted 5-3 in favor of the development, but the concerns that the area is not suitable for the increased traffic remain for some.
